# hosttracker_monitors (Data Source)

Reads the account's monitors, narrowed by the filters below. The filters are ANDed, and each list filter matches any of its values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every production monitor that is currently down.
data "hosttracker_monitors" "down_in_prod" {
  tag   = ["prod"]
  state = ["down"]
}

output "down_urls" {
  value = [for m in data.hosttracker_monitors.down_in_prod.monitors : m.url]
}

# Every http monitor, with its settings read as well.
data "hosttracker_monitors" "web" {
  type             = ["http"]
  include_settings = true
  max_results      = 500
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `include_settings` (Boolean) Also read each monitor's settings into `settings_json`. Off by default: settings are the expensive part of a listing.
- `max_results` (Number) How many monitors to collect across pages. Defaults to 1000. The data source walks the cursor itself and stops here.
- `q` (String) Keep only monitors whose name or address contains this text, matched case-insensitively.
- `state` (Set of String) Keep only monitors in these states: `up`, `down`, `paused`, `maintenance`.
- `tag` (Set of String) Keep only monitors carrying any of these tags, matched exactly.
- `type` (Set of String) Keep only monitors of these types. An unknown type is refused rather than answered with an empty list.

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) The matched monitors' ids, in the order the API returned them.
- `monitors` (Attributes List) The matched monitors. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors))

<a id="nestedatt--monitors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors`

Read-Only:

- `created` (Number) When the monitor was created, in Unix seconds.
- `cron_schedule` (String) The cron expression, when the monitor is cron-scheduled.
- `effective_url` (String) The normalized address actually monitored.
- `enabled` (Boolean) The configured enablement flag.
- `full_log` (Boolean) Whether every check is recorded.
- `id` (String) The monitor's id.
- `interval` (Number) The check interval, in seconds.
- `locations` (Attributes) Where the check runs from. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors--locations))
- `name` (String) The display name.
- `open_stat` (Boolean) Whether the statistics are publicly readable.
- `recheck` (Attributes) The quorum rule applied before a failure concludes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors--recheck))
- `settings_json` (String) The monitor's whole settings object as JSON. Empty when the read did not ask for settings.
- `since` (Number) When the current state began, in Unix seconds.
- `sla_target` (Number) The uptime percentage the monitor is measured against.
- `state` (String) `up`, `down`, `paused` or `maintenance`.
- `tags` (Set of String) The monitor's tags.
- `type` (String) Which kind of check this is.
- `updated` (Number) The API's change marker, in Unix seconds.
- `url` (String) The address the check is aimed at, as it was written.

<a id="nestedatt--monitors--locations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors.locations`

Read-Only:

- `excluded_agents` (Set of String) Locations explicitly kept off this check.
- `fallback` (String) What happens when no chosen location is available.
- `pools` (Set of String) The monitoring-location pools.


<a id="nestedatt--monitors--recheck"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors.recheck`

Read-Only:

- `min_num_down` (Number) How many locations must report a failure.
- `strategy` (String) The quorum rule.
